thesis: Beauty’s economy combines produced experience, transmitted information, positional advantage and capture of income.

ideas.statement: Aesthetic value can be real while rewards reflect mistaken inference or positional competition; gains must be separated from who captures them.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Observational wage studies do not isolate universal premiums; the maze experiment shows particular channels, and defensive-spending races are models rather than all grooming.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Observational wage studies do not isolate universal premiums; the maze experiment shows particular channels, and defensive-spending races are models rather than all grooming.

audit.notes: Direct active-LLM analysis; argument distinguished from established empirical result.
